Looters had used tools to undercut the flood-shorn riverbanks, leaving holes big enough to stand in.

  The three researchers and 10 MTSU students spent six months surveying 128 riverbank or bank line sites and documenting samples from the 20 most endangered. Student Joey Keasler says he was shocked at the sight of bones scattered like trash along the water’s edge. “The looters just hack into the soil with picks and shovels,” he says, “and if they find human remains, they just toss them over their shoulder.”

 With little law enforcement devoted to fighting a “victimless crime,” public vigilance may be the best protector of the Cumberland’s shell middens. Despite their vulnerability, Peres says she won’t excavate an entire site unless it is threatened by development. His sons, Marcus junior and Samuel Samuel, inherited the business and expanded it, becoming interested in the oil export business. They commissioned the world's first purpose-built oil tanker, the Murex, which in 1892 made its first voyage. In 1897, the brothers renamed their business The "Shell" Transport and Trading Company. Meanwhile, a rival firm, the Royal Dutch Petroleum Company, was established in the Netherlands in 1890 to develop an oilfield in Sumatra. Both companies were competing with the dominant American player, Standard Oil. Facing intense competition and overproduction in the market, the two decided to join forces. A pivotal moment came in April 1907 when Shell Transport and Trading merged with Royal Dutch Petroleum. This created the Royal Dutch Shell Group, with ownership split 60/40 between the Dutch and British entities, respectively. This structure allowed the combined company to compete on a global scale. The new group expanded rapidly, opening operations across Europe and Asia. For nearly a century, this dual-company structure remained. However, in 2005, following a reserves-overstatement controversy, the partnership was dissolved and unified into a single new holding company, Royal Dutch Shell plc, to improve efficiency and simplify its corporate structure. Our brand history

Since the first use of the Shell name at the end of the 19 th Century, the brand has grown to become one of the most well-recognised in the world. In this section, you can follow that evolution from humble beginnings to household name.

1890 – 1907

The Shell name

The origin of the Shell name can be traced back to the seashells that Marcus Samuel senior imported from the Far East during the late 19th Century. When his sons Marcus junior and Samuel were looking for a name for the kerosene that they were exporting to Asia, they chose Shell.
As kerosene sales came to dominate the business’s turnover, the name was adopted for the new import-export organisation that was set up in 1897 – the Shell Transport and Trading company.
The Shell name briefly took a back seat in 1907 when the company was merged with Royal Dutch to form, the Royal Dutch Shell Group, but the newly formed business quickly became known as Shell for short.

The Shell logo

Shell’s yellow and red scallop shell logo is one of the most recognisable symbols in the world, but it actually started life as a black and white mussel shell. This design was trademarked in 1900 and is the oldest of 22,000+ trademarks owned by Shell.
